previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including type 1 diabetes, pancreas transplant, end-stage renal disease on peritoneal dialysis, chronic heart failure, and severe orthostatic hypotension was admitted for chills, low-grade fever, and hypotension. She was found to have stable vital signs without evidence of active infection, as blood, urine, and peritoneal fluid cultures were negative. Her hypotension was attributed to excessive fluid removal during peritoneal dialysis, and antibiotics were discontinued after no infectious source was identified. Imaging showed pleural effusions and pulmonary edema, with echocardiography revealing moderate to severe mitral regurgitation and reduced left ventricular function. Her CD4 count was low at 165, but she remained on appropriate prophylactic medications. Warfarin was adjusted to 1 mg daily due to prior supratherapeutic INR and ongoing clotting risk. She improved clinically, was weaned off vasopressors, and transitioned back to extended care with follow-up planned in cardiology for mitral valve evaluation.

SUMMARY: Ms. ___ is a ___ with multiple end-stage 
complications from type I diabetes including nephropathy ___ 
renal transplant and renal-pancreas transplant and currently on 
peritoneal dialysis who was referred for admission from her 
dialysis center with symptomatic hypotension (SBP in ___. Blood 
pressures responded to a 500 cc fluid bolus and remained stable 
at her baseline of SBPs ___. She was followed in-house by 
her nephrologist Dr. ___ his team, who recommended 
changes to her dialysate to limit excessive fluid removal.

ACTIVE ISSUES:

# HYPOTENSION: Ms. ___ was referred to the ED for 
evaluation of symptomatic hypotension. Her blood pressure was as 
low as SBPs in the ___, which is below her baseline of SBPs 
___. Blood pressure normalized to her baseline after a 
500-cc fluid bolus, suggesting that the acute decrease in 
pressure was most likely secondary to hypovolemia from fluid 
shifts with peritoneal dialysis. This was her second such 
admission with similar presentation in less than a month.  There 
was a low suspicion for sepsis as a cause, though she was 
started on levofloxacin for ? infiltrate on chest x-ray and 
contribution from concurrent infection cannot be ruled out.  She 
is also symptomatic from baseline hypotension, which is likely 
multifactorial, due to a combination of her dysautonomia from 
diabetic nephropathy, volume shifts with peritoneal dialysis, 
systolic heart failure, and orthostasis from deconditioning and 
spending most of her time in the bed.  She was continued on her 
home medications of midodrine, fludricortisone, and salt tabs, 
and changes to her dialysis regimen were made as below with a 
goal of maintaining her slightly more ""wet"" to limit symptomatic 
hypotension. However, this may lead to complications from heart 
failure given her sensitive volume status.  She will require 
close monitoring by her cardiologist Dr. ___ 
nephrologist Dr. ___ forward; they will be in ongoing 
communication.

# ESRD ON PERITONEAL DIALYSIS: She was followed in-house by the 
nephrology consult team led by her primary nephrologist Dr. 
___. Her PD regimen was adjusted to:

a. Number of dwells in 24h: 4
b. Dextrose 1.5% for three dwells, 2.5% for the fourth
c. Volume of each dwell: 2L
d. Duration of each dwell: 3h
e. After the last of 4 dwells, please fill with 2L of 1.5% and 
leave alone until the start of the next cycle
f. please record volumes, daily weights, turbidity in bedside 
flow sheet

This resulted in a net positive fluid balance of 100-200 cc per 
session, consistent with the goal of avoiding excessive fluid 
removal. She was continued on calcium acetate and calcitriol. 

# ? RESPIRATORY INFECTION: A PA & lateral chest film was 
obtained (prelinary read as above) showing worsening effusions 
and ? infiltrate. Given that the patient was reporting worsened 
cough and some pleuritic pain at the left chest, she was started 
on levofloxacin for a planned ___ course. She did not develop 
fever or white count, though these signs may be suppressed in 
this patient with known immunosuppression and immune system 
dysfunction.

# HYPOTHYROIDISM: The patient has reported low mood and energy 
recently, and so her TSH was rechecked and returned at 26. Her 
levothyroxine was therefore increased from 150 mcg to 175 mcg 
daily.  TSH should be rechecked in ___ weeks.

discharge with foul odor. She reported history of similar 
symptoms which were responsive to metronidazole; therefore she 
was treated empirically and should complete a ___ course of

site of suture removal on her hand. She will follow up in hand 
clinic as an outpatient.  She will also follow up with podiatry 
to have her toenails trimmed and address skin care for her foot.

___ emphasized her preference to continue with careful 
positioning to minimize pressure over sacral ulcer. She would 
like to continue with the Mepilex foam, which she believes is 
helpful.  She also requests elbow pads to minimize risk of 
developing pressure ulcers on her elbows when propping herself 
to sit. She requests documentation of the fact that Immodium is 
beneficial to her in reducing her chronic diarrhea and secondary 
complications of skin breakdown. 

INACTIVE ISSUES:

# TYPE I DIABETES, ___ RENAL-PANCREAS TRANSPLANT: Complicated by 
nephropathy, retinopathy, neuropathy.  The patient was continued 
on immunosuppressants prednisone and tacrolimus and prophylaxis 
with acyclovir, fluconazole and atovaquone. Home medications of 
Creon 12 and lactase were modified according to hospital

neuropathy.

# HEMATOLOGIC: Followed by Dr. ___. Has unusual CD4 
lymphopenia which may represent an adverse reaction to MMF (now 
stopped). Also has anemia secondary to renal failure. She was 
continued on home medications of cyanocobalamin, iron, epoetin 
alfa, and folic acid. On antimicrobial prophylaxis as above.

# OPHTHALMOLOGIC: The patient was continued on her home eye 
drops or hospital formulary equivalents. Of note, she reported 
that the dorzolamide was intended to be prescribed twice daily 
by her ophthalmologist so this dose adjustment was made; this is 
consistent with documentation in the inpatient ophthalmology 
consult note from her last admission.

# CAD ___ CABG, ISCHEMIC CARDIOMYOPATHY WITH EF 35%: After

changes to her dialysis made with the intent of improving her

aspirin, and warfarin. INR was therapeutic during this 
admission. 

# CHRONIC DIARRHEA: Possibly secondary to ischemic colitis. No 
blood in stool. She was continued on closest hospital equivalent 
to Preparation H, loperamide and simethicone.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  Severe type 1 diabetes mellitus, end-stage renal disease on
peritoneal dialysis, now status post pancreatic transplant on
immunosuppression, admitted with hypotension, has some dullness at left base
on exam.  Evaluate fluid status, infiltrate at left base?

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior radiographs of the chest, the most recent
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Upright PA and lateral radiographs of the chest.

FINDINGS/IMPRESSION:  Median sternotomy wires are intact, and there is a
prosthetic mitral valve.  Cardiomegaly is unchanged.  The mediastinal
silhouette is normal.  A small right pleural effusion is new and the moderate
left pleural effusion is slightly larger.  Consolidation of the left lower
lung suggests atelectasis; however, underlying infection cannot be excluded. 
There is no pneumothorax.  A hiatal hernia appears grossly unchanged. 

IMPRESSION: 
1.  New small right pleural effusion.  Moderate left pleural effusion, which
is slightly larger compared to prior. 

2.  Worsening consolidation of the left lower lung suggests atelectasis,
underlying infection not excluded.
